ArticleFlux Broadcast — powered by FluxCast. Read to me turns the slideshow into a narrated programme: your feed, written as a bulletin and read over music. Everything it depends on is here, with what is on and what is not.
▶

Read to me needs a few things on

Each switch takes effect as soon as you press it and is saved to your account, so it is the same on every device you sign in on.
Smart+ voiceThe browser's own voice reads the page, so it can't speak a written segment or say where it has got to. Sends article text to OpenAI.
An OpenAI key on the serverSet by whoever runs this server, not from here.
ready
▤

The narration

The narrator's manner, the music under it, and whether each article is summarised instead of read in full.
How it soundsThe narrator's manner. All four say the same facts — they differ in pace, in sentence length, and in how much they tell you what a story is worth. None of them invents anything: an opinion about how much a result matters is allowed, a fact that is not in the article is not.
Opening sting and musicThree notes when the broadcast starts — they fill the pause while the first segment is being written — and a track underneath it afterwards, quiet enough to sit under speech. The music is only downloaded when you first play it, and only the piece you chose. The opening notes are picked at random each broadcast, not from this list — a different one most evenings is expected, not a bug.
Summarise before readingNo effect while “Join the stories up” is on, because a broadcast segment is already the short version. Your choice is kept for when it is off.
The broadcast rewrites each article so it hands over from the one before it. That sends article text to OpenAI and costs money on the account this server uses.
